ai.text:
The European Parliament has approved, by 580 votes to 51 with 39 abstentions, a change to EU law that brings into EU rules a set of fishing conservation and management measures adopted in 2021 and 2022 by the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM), a body the EU has been part of since 1998. The aim is to apply these measures fully and on time, so the EU meets its international commitments and gives fishing operators clear and predictable rules that apply the same way across the EU. The amended text stresses that the measures should be transposed strictly, so that all operators compete on equal terms without being asked to meet obligations beyond those the GFCM recommendations actually set.

The measures cover a wide range of areas. They include new fisheries restricted areas in the Jabuka/Pomo Pit in the Adriatic Sea and in the Gulf of Lion, to protect spawning fish and sensitive deep-sea habitats. Other measures set rules for sprat and piked dogfish fishing in the Black Sea, reduce the impact of fishing on sea turtles, whales and dolphins, and sharks and rays in the Mediterranean, and introduce a catch certificate scheme for turbot in the Black Sea. There are also measures to tackle illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, including a list of vessels presumed to have carried out such fishing, along with management plans for several species and areas, such as small pelagic fish in the Adriatic, red coral, blackspot seabream, demersal fish and shrimp in various Mediterranean areas, and the European eel. Minimum rules for recreational fishing in the Mediterranean and joint inspection and surveillance schemes in the Strait of Sicily and the Ionian Sea are also included.

To reduce plastic pollution, fish aggregating devices (FADs) must be made only from biodegradable materials from 15 August 2027, so that any that are lost do not add to marine plastic. The Commission is also empowered to adopt delegated acts to update several existing GFCM-based rules, covering matters such as the vessel register, derogations for red coral, catch documentation schemes for red coral and turbot, port state measures, the maps and coordinates of the GFCM subareas, and port inspection procedures and transshipment declarations.
